summary: The article surveys fast-growing markets for health and wellness products, driven by a consumer shift from reactive health care to proactive wellness since September 2023. It profiles companies in supplements, wearables, apps, organic goods, nutraceuticals, mental health and sustainable products, and highlights technology's role and the growth of organic and mental-health segments. It concludes that demand will keep growing as the industry becomes more holistic.
one_line: Overview of booming health and wellness markets, from AI supplements and wearables to organic, nutraceutical, mental health and sustainable products, with company profiles.
key_facts: Natasha Richardson, a health trends analyst, said at the Global Wellness Summit on October 14, 2023 that people have moved from reactive health strategies to proactive wellness plans.
VitaHealth was established by Michael Thompson in January 2024 and uses an AI algorithm to tailor vitamins and minerals to individual health data.
Pure Harmony was launched by former Olympic athlete Chloe Martin and offers supplements and health snacks for professional athletes, now also used by fitness enthusiasts.
LifeSync, led by Rajesh Singh, makes wearables that track fitness metrics and give insights into stress management and mental wellness.
TechHealth Solutions' market analysis reports a 180% increase in the use of personal health apps since September 2023.

The MindMatters app, introduced on November 1, 2023, was created by neuroscientist Dr. Emily Stuart and entrepreneur David Weiss and offers cognitive behavioral therapy and personalized mindfulness sessions.
Demand for organic and natural products is forecasted to drive billions in annual sales by late 2025.
Green Essence, founded by siblings Maria and Tomas Gonzalez from a small family farm, provides organic skincare and homeopathic remedies with community-based sourcing.
Champion Nutritionals develops nutraceuticals for joint health and cognitive function, with R&D led by Chief Scientist Dr. Anita Desai.
Lumina Therapy, whose CEO is clinical psychologist Christine Liu, offers a digital therapeutic platform with personalized therapy modules.
EcoWell, under CEO Jessica Teng, makes sustainably produced products such as yoga mats and water bottles in eco-friendly packaging.
The article describes a market pivot from physical wellness toward mental and emotional health.
